scenario: AITA for telling my mom she was a bad mother? | So this is kind of a two part thing. A while back, I made my mother upset because of a couple different things I said while out with her. She was saying something about how she didn't believe in doctors and that my siblings literally beg her to go and she still puts off taking them as long as possible. I told her that's not okay, that she did that to me and I nearly died (I was hospitalized for weeks, and spent several months on bedrest recovering), and that if she keeps that up one of us really might die some day because of her. She didn't take that too well, but ended up dropping it and brushing it off as no big deal. Later on, she asked me to go grab her a drink and when I asked her what she wanted she said "well you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" And I told her no, I do not know what you like, my grandparents raised me, I still don't know anything about you. She got upset and started crying and said "what's your problem!? This is the second time today that you've been mean to me and tried to make me seem like a bad person!" I told her I'm not trying to be mean I was just saying it's not cool to not take your kid to the doctor and that I'm not going to know anything about her since I didnt grow up with her. We ended up going home shortly after and went out again the other night, a few weeks later. Well I got my brother a phone because they kept taking his (that a different family member pays for) and I wanted him to have his own, so I made it clear they can keep his other one and this one is STRICTLY for him. Well I found out they've been taking and using this one too, so when I saw her I told her, seriously, I dont want to take the phone back because I don't want him to be punished for what you're doing, but I will take it back if you don't stop stealing it from him. That is HIS that I'M paying for, not you, it is not yours to touch, it's already bad enough that you keep all his work money at least don't touch his phone. She got upset and starting yelling and crying saying I need to stop treating her like a bad mother, and I told her well to be honest she kind of IS one. She had a meltdown and started sobbing and said well fine, I don't need you in my life anyways, and left without me. Now my family is saying I shouldn't of treated her like that even if she wasn't that great to me. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to tell my mom that she's a bad mother. Let me start by understanding the situation better. From what I gather, there were a couple of incidents where I said things to my mom that upset her. The first time was when she was talking about not believing in doctors and how she put off taking my siblings and me to the doctor, even when they begged her. I told her that's not okay because she did that to me, and I nearly died because of it. I was hospitalized for weeks and had to spend several months on bed rest recovering. I was worried that if she kept doing that, one of us might die someday because of her actions. She didn't take it well but eventually dropped the subject. Then, later that day, she asked me to grab her a drink, and when I asked what she wanted, she said, "Well, you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" I responded by saying I don't know what she likes because my grandparents raised me, and I still don't know anything about her. She got upset, started crying, and asked, "What's your problem? This is the second time today that you've been mean to me and tried to make me seem like a bad person!" I tried to explain that I wasn't trying to be mean, just saying it's not cool to not take the kids to the doctor and that I don't know anything about her since I didn't grow up with her. We ended up going home shortly after. A few weeks later, we went out again. I had gotten my brother a phone because they kept taking his (which a different family member pays for), and I wanted him to have his own. I made it clear they can keep his other one, and this one is STRICTLY for him. But I found out they've been taking and using this one too. When I saw her, I told her seriously that I don't want to take the phone back because I don't want him to be punished for what she's doing, but I will take it back if she doesn't stop stealing it from him. I explained that it's HIS phone that I'm paying for, not hers, and it's already bad enough that she keeps all his work money, so at least don't touch his phone. She got upset, started yelling and crying, saying I need to stop treating her like a bad mother, and I told her, well to be honest, she kind of IS one. She had a meltdown, started sobbing, and said, "Well fine, I don't need you in my life anyway," and left without me. Now, my family is saying I shouldn't have treated her like that, even if she wasn't that great to me. So, the question is, AITA? Am I the one at fault here? First, I need to understand what AITA means. From what I know, AITA stands for "Am I the Asshole?" It's a way to ask if you're being unreasonable or unfair in a situation. So, in this case, I'm asking if I was the asshole for telling my mom she's a bad mother. To figure this out, I need to look at the situation from different angles. Let's start by considering the context of our relationship. It seems like there's a history of issues between us. She didn't take me to the doctor when I was a child, which had serious consequences for me. That's a significant issue because it directly impacted my health and well-being. I nearly died because of her actions, which is a heavy burden to carry. Then, in the first incident, I confronted her about not taking the kids to the doctor. I told her that's not okay and that if she keeps doing that, one of us might die. She didn't take it well but eventually dropped the subject. I tried to explain that I wasn't trying to be mean, just stating my concerns about her not taking the kids to the doctor and that I don't know much about her since I didn't grow up with her. In the third incident, I gave my brother a phone, and she started using it without permission. I confronted her about it, explaining that it's my brother's phone, and I don't want him to be punished for her actions. I told her I'll take it back if she doesn't stop stealing it. She got upset, started yelling and crying, and accused me of treating her like a bad mother. I responded by saying she kind of IS one, which led to her leaving without me. Now, my family is saying I shouldn't have treated her like that, even if she wasn't that great to me. So, the question is, was I the asshole for telling her she's a bad mother? However, the way I expressed my concerns might have been harsh. Telling her that if she keeps doing that, one of us might die is a strong statement. While it's understandable that I'm upset and concerned, the way I expressed it could have been more compassionate. In the second incident, her comment about me knowing what she likes because she's raised me for 26 years was insensitive, especially considering that my grandparents raised me. My response was honest but perhaps a bit blunt. In the third incident, she started using my brother's phone without permission. Finally, my family's perspective is that I shouldn't have treated her like that, even if she wasn't that great to me.
